phase_goal: A Next 16 skeleton a developer can run locally end-to-end (pnpm dev against local Supabase Docker) with Sentry + PostHog wired and verified, security headers applied, closed error-code registry in place, and ci.yml running lint + typecheck + Vitest unit + integration + local-build Playwright smoke. No Vercel, no preview URLs, no deploy workflows, no Inngest yet.
canonical_refs: docs/CAVE-PRD.md §20 (Environments + CI/CD + env vars + local dev commands)
CLAUDE.md (stack lock-in — Next 16.2.3, React 19.2.5, Serwist 9.5.7, Sentry 10.48.0, PostHog 1.368.0, next-intl 4.9.1, Vitest 4.1.4, Playwright 1.59.1)
prior_decisions: Stack locked in CLAUDE.md: Next 16 App Router + React 19 + TS strict + @serwist/next PWA
Local DB: Supabase CLI Docker stack (supabase start / supabase db reset)
Observability: Sentry (release=git SHA, source maps post-build) + PostHog US cloud
Error codes: closed registry from PRD §5 — no ad-hoc codes
Locale: pt-BR only, next-intl day one, <html lang='pt-BR'>
Testing: Vitest unit + integration against real Postgres (no mocking), Playwright smoke
Inngest/Resend/Stripe deferred to their first-consumer phases (4, 10) — NOT onboarded here
Vercel hosting + deploy pipeline deferred to Phase 12 — NOT set up here (ci.yml only)

questions.title: Node version pin
questions.context: Next 16 requires Node ≥18.18; stack lock doesn't specify. Developer + CI must agree on version. .nvmrc + engines field keeps everyone aligned.

options.label: Node 22 LTS (.nvmrc + engines)
options.description: Current LTS as of 2026. Future-proof. Some ecosystem lag possible.

options.label: Node 20 LTS (.nvmrc + engines)
options.description: Previous LTS, widely deployed. Mature npm ecosystem. Supported until 2026-04.

options.label: No pin, document minimum in README
options.description: Lightweight. Drift risk between local and CI.

questions.chat_more: make sure you create the .nvmrc file locally

questions.title: pnpm version activation
questions.context: pnpm is the chosen package manager. Version pinning keeps CI + devs lockstep on lockfile format. Corepack is shipped with Node.

options.label: Corepack + packageManager field
options.description: Node-native: `packageManager: pnpm@9.x.y` in package.json; Corepack auto-installs matching version. No extra tool to install.

options.label: Global pnpm, documented minimum
options.description: README tells dev to `npm i -g pnpm@9`. Simple but manual.

options.label: Volta for the whole toolchain
options.description: Volta pins Node + pnpm + eslint together. Extra install step but strongest reproducibility.

questions.title: Linter & formatter
questions.context: Next 16 ships with an ESLint flat-config by default. Formatter choice is independent. Biome is a faster all-in-one alternative.

options.label: ESLint (Next flat config) + Prettier
options.description: Mainstream, huge plugin ecosystem, works with every IDE out of the box. Two tools to configure.

options.label: Biome (lint + format single tool)
options.description: Fast (Rust), single config. Smaller rule coverage vs ESLint, fewer plugins.

options.label: ESLint + typescript-eslint strict + Prettier
options.description: Adds strict TS lint ruleset on top of option a. Catches more bugs, slower lint runs, more churn.

questions.title: Git hooks & commit linting
questions.context: Hooks enforce format/lint pre-commit so bad code never lands. Commit linting enforces Conventional Commits for changelog/SemVer automation.

options.label: Husky + lint-staged (no commitlint)
options.description: Pre-commit format + lint on staged files only. Commit style loose.

options.label: Husky + lint-staged + commitlint
options.description: Enforces Conventional Commits. Good for automated release notes; friction for ad-hoc commits.

options.label: simple-git-hooks + lint-staged
options.description: Lighter than Husky (no runtime dep), same outcome for pre-commit.

options.label: No hooks, rely on CI
options.description: Less friction locally. Bad code gets caught in CI instead of at commit time.

questions.title: Task runner / script convention
questions.context: Multi-step dev commands (start Supabase + app, reset DB, run test suites) benefit from named shortcuts. npm scripts are universal but verbose for orchestrated flows.

options.label: npm scripts only
options.description: Zero new deps. `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm db:reset` — all in package.json scripts.

options.label: npm scripts + justfile
options.description: Just (Rust task runner) for multi-step flows; pnpm scripts call `just`. Cleaner for complex recipes.

options.label: npm scripts + turbo
options.description: Turbo adds build caching + task orchestration. Overkill for a single package but forward-looking if you split into packages.

questions.title: TS strictness flags
questions.context: INFRA-01 locks `strict: true` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Additional flags surface more subtle bugs at the cost of some friction.

options.label: Locked minimum only
options.description: `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Simplest, minimal friction.

options.label: + exactOptionalPropertyTypes + noImplicitOverride
options.description: Catches `undefined` vs missing-property mix-ups and accidental override mistakes.

options.label: + exactOptional + noImplicitOverride + noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature
options.description: Strictest reasonable set. Forces `obj['foo']` over `obj.foo` for dynamic indexes — noisier but surfaces unchecked access.

questions.title: Path aliases in tsconfig
questions.context: PRD §2 mandates src/contexts/... + src/shared/.... Aliases determine how imports read.

options.label: Single alias `@/*` → `src/*`
options.description: Next.js default. Imports look like `import { x } from '@/contexts/iam/...'`. Simplest config.

options.label: Per-root aliases `@contexts/*` + `@shared/*`
options.description: Explicit per-root. Imports read as `import { x } from '@contexts/iam/...'`. Highlights the architectural split.

options.label: Both
options.description: `@/*` for general + `@contexts/*`, `@shared/*` for named roots. Flexible but more to maintain.

questions.title: Barrel files per context
questions.context: `index.ts` re-exports can enable `import { User } from '@contexts/iam'` — but too many barrels cause cycles and hurt tree-shaking.

options.label: No barrels — direct imports everywhere
options.description: Avoids cycles, best tree-shaking. Imports are longer (`.../domain/user.ts`). Safest.

options.label: Barrel at context root only
options.description: Each context exports its public API via `src/contexts/iam/index.ts`. Cross-context imports go through the barrel; intra-context imports stay direct.

options.label: Barrels at every layer
options.description: domain/index.ts + application/index.ts etc. Most ergonomic imports; highest cycle risk.

questions.title: Bounded-context scaffold depth at Phase 1
questions.context: PRD §2 locks 7 contexts × 5 layers + 5 shared subdirs = 40 folders. Phase 2 fills db/adapters; Phases 4+ fill feature code. What ships at Phase 1?

options.label: Empty folders with .gitkeep only
options.description: Just establish the shape so later phases have landing zones. Smallest footprint.

options.label: Folders + README.md per context
options.description: Each context README describes aggregates, emits, consumes (copied from PRD §3). Serves as an onboarding + guardrail doc.

options.label: Folders + README + layer-marker stub files
options.description: Adds e.g. `domain/_layer.md` explaining what belongs in this layer. Strongest guardrail; more files to maintain.

questions.title: Error-code registry shape
questions.context: PRD §5 defines 20 error codes as the CLOSED set. INFRA-20 requires this as a single importable source of truth. Every route handler imports from it.

options.label: TypeScript `enum`
options.description: `export enum ErrorCode { Unauthenticated = 'unauthenticated', ... }`. Familiar. Has known runtime/emit quirks in TS.

options.label: `as const` object + string-literal union
options.description: `export const ErrorCode = { ... } as const; export type ErrorCode = (typeof ErrorCode)[keyof typeof ErrorCode]`. Tree-shakeable, ESM-friendly, no enum footguns.

options.label: Discriminated union per code
options.description: Each code paired with its required detail shape. Richer typing; much more verbose; overkill for a flat registry.

questions.title: Error response body shape
questions.context: Clients need a consistent shape. PRD §5 gives codes + HTTP statuses but no JSON shape. Phase 6's confidence ladder, Phase 9's offline queue, Phase 10's paywall all consume this shape.

options.label: `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`
options.description: Nested error object. Common REST convention. Leaves top-level for success fields.

options.label: `{ code, message, details? }`
options.description: Flat. Distinguishes success vs error by HTTP status + presence of `code`. Simpler client-side.

options.label: RFC 7807 problem+json
options.description: `{ type, title, status, code, detail, instance? }`. Standards-based. More verbose; most tooling compatible.

questions.title: Location of the error-code registry
questions.context: Every context will import this. Location signals whether it's config, infra, or telemetry.

options.label: `src/shared/errors/{registry.ts, response.ts}`
options.description: Own top-level module. Clear purpose: error codes + HTTP mapping.

options.label: `src/shared/config/errors.ts`
options.description: Co-located with other config (env, feature flags). Smaller module surface.

options.label: `src/shared/telemetry/errors.ts`
options.description: Bundled with Sentry filter config so the scrub rules + registry live together.

questions.title: Serwist setup depth at Phase 1
questions.context: @serwist/next locked. Phase 3 (Design System) ships the full offline shell + app-update toast + installable manifest. What does Phase 1 need to prove?

options.label: Skeleton — registered SW, no precache, no offline page
options.description: Proves Serwist builds + registers. Nothing functional yet. Least churn for Phase 3 to rewrite.

options.label: Basic — fallback /offline route + precache of `/`
options.description: Minimal offline works today. Phase 3 themes + expands the precache. Intermediate risk of churn.

options.label: Full runtime caching rules ready
options.description: Everything Phase 3 would need. Risks Phase 1 making calls about caching strategy before the design system exists.

questions.title: Web app manifest at Phase 1
questions.context: Full manifest (icons, theme colors, screenshots) lands in Phase 3 with the Paper Cream design system. Phase 1 needs at least enough for Serwist to not complain.

options.label: Minimal placeholder (name, display, theme_color)
options.description: `{ name, short_name, display: 'standalone', theme_color: '#000001' }` — no icons. Phase 3 rewrites. Smallest footprint.

options.label: Full structure, placeholder assets
options.description: All icon slots filled with placeholder PNGs (e.g. solid color). Phase 3 swaps assets, not manifest structure. Less churn.

options.label: No manifest at Phase 1
options.description: Defer entirely to Phase 3. Serwist still builds (manifest is declarative), but installability is deferred.

questions.title: next-intl routing strategy
questions.context: pt-BR only at launch. PLATFORM-v2-03 (additional locales) is deferred but the i18n layer is mandatory day one.

options.label: No locale prefix (single-locale mode)
options.description: URLs stay clean: `/catalog` not `/pt-BR/catalog`. When v2 adds locales, migration requires URL redesign.

options.label: `as-needed` prefix (default locale hidden)
options.description: pt-BR served at root, future locales get `/en-US/...`. next-intl's recommended default. No URL migration when adding locales.

options.label: Always prefix (`/pt-BR/...`)
options.description: Most explicit. Uglier URLs now; zero migration risk later.

questions.title: Supabase CLI version pinning
questions.context: Local dev (INFRA-26) and future Phase 12 CI share the CLI. Drift between versions can break the local stack or branch-DB workflow.

options.label: Pin via `supabase/config.toml` + README install cmd
options.description: supabase CLI itself isn't in npm by default; config.toml declares expected version. Developers install matching. Phase 12 CI uses same pin via brew/download.

options.label: npm devDependency (`supabase` package)
options.description: `pnpm supabase ...` runs via the project's locked version. Everyone matches the lockfile automatically. The `supabase` npm package is the official wrapper.

options.label: No pin — use whatever's globally installed
options.description: Simplest. Breaks on drift. Not recommended.

questions.title: DB seed convention at Phase 1
questions.context: `supabase db reset` runs migrations + seed. No migrations yet (Phase 2 lands the schema). Phase 1 just needs the seed contract to exist.

options.label: Empty `supabase/seed.sql` stub with comment
options.description: File exists so `supabase db reset` works; Phase 2 adds schema + seed rows. Lowest Phase 1 effort.

options.label: Per-context seed files composed into master
options.description: `supabase/seed/{iam,catalog,...}.sql` sourced from `supabase/seed.sql`. Forward-looking structure; Phase 1 writes empty files.

options.label: No seed file at Phase 1
options.description: Defer entirely to Phase 2. `supabase db reset` works without a seed file.

questions.title: How the app reads local Supabase URLs
questions.context: `supabase start` outputs the local DB URL, anon key, service role key. App needs DATABASE_URL + NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in `.env.local`.

options.label: Manual — README documents copying from `supabase status` into `.env.local`
options.description: One-time setup step per machine. Fragile if local Supabase rotates keys.

options.label: Automated script `scripts/sync-supabase-env.sh`
options.description: Parses `supabase status` and writes `.env.local`. Devs run once per fresh-start. Scripted = reproducible.

options.label: `supabase gen` or `supabase init` CLI-native flow
options.description: Use whatever the Supabase CLI itself provides for env sync. Depends on CLI version features.

questions.title: Local-dev Sentry strategy
questions.context: CONFLICT to resolve: PRD §20 table says Sentry 'disabled' locally. But Phase 1 success criterion 4 says 'a deliberately thrown error in the local app appears in Sentry'. Same conflict applies to PostHog (Q-20).

options.label: Disabled locally; verification only in CI Playwright smoke
options.description: CI sets SENTRY_DSN pointing to a `folhario-dev` project; Playwright triggers the error, asserts the event lands. Local dev never pings Sentry. Strictly matches PRD §20.

options.label: Enabled locally in a shared `folhario-dev` project
options.description: Devs can eyeball their own scrubbing + breadcrumbs. Noisier project; easier to catch regressions.

options.label: Opt-in local via SENTRY_ENABLED_LOCAL=true env
options.description: Default off (matches PRD §20). Flip when verifying scrubbing or debugging. Best of both.

questions.title: Local-dev PostHog strategy
questions.context: Same conflict. Phase 1 success criterion 4 says client + posthog-node server pings must fire and be verified by Playwright smoke.

options.label: Disabled locally; CI-only verification
options.description: Mirrors Q-19a. CI feeds POSTHOG_API_KEY for a dev project; Playwright asserts the capture network call.

options.label: Enabled locally in `folhario-dev` project
options.description: Dev events pollute the project but give instant feedback.

options.label: Opt-in local via POSTHOG_ENABLED_LOCAL=true
options.description: Default off, flip on demand. Pairs naturally with Q-19c.

questions.title: PostHog autocapture setting
questions.context: Autocapture records $pageview, $click, $rageclick automatically — can include button text, input values, form field names. PRD §20 defines an explicit event taxonomy. LGPD-13 bans PII in telemetry.

options.label: Disable autocapture — explicit events only
options.description: Only the PRD §20 taxonomy events fire. Smallest payload, safest LGPD stance, less debugging data.

options.label: Enable autocapture with strict masking
options.description: `mask_all_text: true`, `mask_all_element_attributes: true`, `disable_session_recording: true`. Get the click graph without content. Some config complexity.

options.label: Enable autocapture default
options.description: Richest data. Highest LGPD risk — may capture form inputs / plant names / notes. Not recommended.

questions.title: Sentry PII scrubbing implementation
questions.context: LGPD-13 + PRD §13.7: scrub `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `email`, `password`, `token`, `photo_url`; DROP request bodies on `/api/v1/identifications/*`; `Sentry.setUser({ id })` only. This needs to be bulletproof — Playwright smoke verifies it.

options.label: SDK built-ins (`denyUrls` + `sendDefaultPii: false`) + minimal `beforeSend`
options.description: Leans on Sentry's default scrubbing. Adds beforeSend hook only for the identification-route body drop. Simplest.

options.label: Centralized custom scrubber module + beforeSend + beforeBreadcrumb
options.description: `src/shared/telemetry/sentry-scrub.ts` owns all regex + route matching. Unit-testable. Pairs with Q-12.

options.label: Server-side data scrubbing (Sentry dashboard config)
options.description: Config in Sentry Project Settings → Data Scrubbing. Easy to tune via UI. Not in repo → not code-reviewable, hard to audit.

questions.title: CSP strategy at Phase 1
questions.context: INFRA-18 / PRD §21: standard security headers via Next.js middleware. PRD lists CSP in the checklist but doesn't specify a policy. CSP is the single biggest security header and the trickiest to get right.

options.label: Strict CSP with per-request nonce
options.description: `script-src 'nonce-{random}' 'strict-dynamic'`. Next.js supports this pattern in middleware. Highest security. May require dev-mode exceptions for Sentry widget, PostHog toolbar.

options.label: Report-only CSP with loose policy
options.description: `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` to a Sentry endpoint. Collect violations without breaking anything; tighten iteratively.

options.label: Skip CSP at Phase 1
options.description: Ship HSTS + XFO + nosniff + Referrer-Policy + Permissions-Policy. CSP lands later when app surface is concrete. Leaves a gap in PRD §21.

questions.chat_more: CSP is a bitch! defer to as late as possible

questions.title: Header set at Phase 1
questions.context: Beyond CSP (Q-23), PRD §21 says 'standard security headers'. Minimum viable vs full defence-in-depth set.

options.label: Minimum — HSTS + X-Frame-Options DENY + X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
options.description: Three most impactful headers. Ship quickly.

options.label: Full set — HSTS + XFO + nosniff + Referrer-Policy + Permissions-Policy
options.description: Adds `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` + `Permissions-Policy` denying unused features (mic, geolocation, etc., camera kept for Phase 6 identify). Best practice.

options.label: Full set + CSP
options.description: Option b plus CSP (pairs with Q-23a or Q-23b). Most defense-in-depth.

questions.chat_more: defer this to the very end if possible

questions.title: Postgres image for integration tests
questions.context: CONFLICT to resolve: Phase 1 success criterion 3 specifies `postgres:17-alpine`. INFRA-12 says `postgres:16-alpine`. PRD §20 says `postgres:16`. Supabase local stack runs Postgres 15 by default. CI should match production — Supabase prod is Postgres 15/16 depending on project age.

options.label: postgres:17-alpine (match ROADMAP success criterion)
options.description: Current stable. Roadmap wins the tie. Diverges from INFRA-12 + Supabase local stack.

options.label: postgres:16-alpine (match INFRA-12 + PRD)
options.description: Aligns with requirements doc + PRD. Closer to Supabase managed versions. Requires ROADMAP success-criterion edit.

options.label: Match local Supabase exactly (currently 15)
options.description: CI mirrors `supabase start` version. Requires bumping both when Supabase CLI upgrades.

questions.chat_more: local supabase uses postgres 17 too. make sure to lock the version locally. also make sure to only enable the needed features.

questions.title: Playwright browsers in CI smoke
questions.context: Folhário is PWA-first → primary users: mobile Chrome (Android), mobile Safari/WebKit (iOS). Adding browsers multiplies CI minutes + flake surface.

options.label: Chromium only
options.description: Fastest CI. Covers ~70% of BR mobile traffic + most desktop. Misses iOS WebKit quirks.

options.label: Chromium + WebKit
options.description: Catches iOS-specific PWA issues (manifest quirks, IndexedDB subtleties). Skips Firefox (<5% BR share).

options.label: All three (Chromium + WebKit + Firefox)
options.description: Most thorough. Slower CI, more flake. Overkill for MVP smoke.

questions.title: What does the Phase 1 Playwright smoke actually assert?
questions.context: Success criterion 4 says Playwright verifies: (1) deliberate error → Sentry with scrubbing, (2) PostHog ping from client + server. How does this work without a full app?

options.label: Dedicated `/__diag` page + `/api/v1/_diagnostics/ping`
options.description: Throwaway diagnostics routes that trigger Sentry.captureException + posthog.capture client-side + posthog-node capture server-side. Playwright intercepts transport calls. Clean separation of concerns.

options.label: Use the home page + a hidden dev-only button
options.description: Button visible only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_DIAGNOSTICS_MODE=true`. Avoids permanent diagnostics routes in the app surface.

options.label: Assert via network interception only
options.description: Playwright loads `/`, mocks window.fetch/XHR to Sentry/PostHog endpoints, asserts calls happen. No app-side code needed. Indirect — tests the mock, not the integration.

questions.chat_more: I don't know, you figure it out

questions.title: CI caching + concurrency
questions.context: Re-running CI across PR pushes should be fast. Caching + concurrency cancellation matter.

options.label: pnpm store + Playwright browsers cached via actions/cache
options.description: Standard pattern. Saves 60-120s per run. Invalidated on lockfile change.

options.label: Option a + GitHub Actions concurrency group per PR
options.description: Cancels previous in-flight runs when a new commit is pushed to the same PR. Saves CI minutes.

options.label: Minimal caching; no concurrency cancellation
options.description: Simpler config. Slower CI, more minutes burned.

questions.title: Typed env validation
questions.context: PRD §20 table has 20+ env vars. Missing or mistyped vars surface as runtime crashes deep in the stack. Fail-fast-at-boot is cheap insurance.

options.label: @t3-oss/env-nextjs + Zod schemas
options.description: Splits server/client vars via NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. Validates at boot. Well-maintained. Extra dep.

options.label: Custom `src/shared/config/env.ts` with Zod
options.description: No extra dep — use the Zod you already have for route bodies. Full control.

options.label: Raw `process.env` with runtime assertions
options.description: Cheapest. No static types for vars. Fragile.

questions.title: .env.example scope at Phase 1
questions.context: .env.example is the developer-onboarding artifact. Including vars for services not yet wired up can confuse or invite misuse.

options.label: All PRD §20 vars with dummy values
options.description: Forward-looking; new contributors see the full surface. May tempt someone to wire up unimplemented services.

options.label: Only Phase 1 vars (Supabase, Sentry, PostHog, IDENTIFICATION_PROVIDER_MODE)
options.description: Clean — matches what's actually wired. Requires updates each phase that adds services.

options.label: No .env.example; README documents instead
options.description: README table is more expressive (add 'when', 'server-only' columns). No file to diff-review when vars change.
